sections.title: Two ways to conjugate the same verb
sections.content: Hungarian verbs conjugate one way when their object is indefinite — a/an, some, or no object at all — and a different way when the object is definite: the, a specific thing already known to both speakers. *Kérek egy kávét* ("I'd like a coffee") uses the indefinite form because *egy kávét* is just any coffee. *Kérem a kávét* ("I'll take the coffee") uses the definite form because *a kávét* is one particular coffee — already on the counter, already ordered, already the one you mean.

sections.title: Indefinite and definite, side by side

sections.content: *Kérem* is the definite form of *kérek*, literally "I ask for [the specific thing you just offered]" — you'll meet it constantly ordering food or shopping, as in *Ezt kérem* ("I'd like this one") or *Kérem a számlát* ("I'll take the bill, please"). The rule of thumb for now: *egy* or no article in front of the object → indefinite (*kérek*, *látok*); *a/az* in front of it → definite (*kérem*, *látom*). The full system has more to it than that, but this covers what you'll actually need for a long time.
